source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 18 October 1946, p. 6 ("Derry elections: nominations for county and rural councils")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Unopposed nominations from the Belfast News-Letter (18 October 1946, p. 6); the same list is in the Derry Journal (18 October 1946, p. 7).

note: Triennial election. The county Londonderry polls were postponed; nominations were taken on 17 October 1946. Portstewart Rural was the only division with two candidates; the other twenty divisions, including Somerset where no nomination was received, were unopposed. Filed on 1946-10-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Londonderry that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1946-10-03 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Ballylaggan' to Ballylagan (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1921-69 (BALLYLAGAN) spell it Ballylagan. This round was filed under the spelling 'Ballylaggan', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (ballylaggan) answers with a redirect to this one.
